chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them):

Regarding a man who divorces a young girl who has not yet reached puberty and is not like her (i.e., not of marriageable age/menstruating), he said: 'There is no waiting period (iddah) upon her, even if he had intercourse with her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the iddah period for a pre-pubescent girl who is divorced?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies that a pre-pubescent girl (al-sabiyah) is exempt from the waiting period (iddah) upon divorce, even if consummation has occurred, as her iddah is primarily tied to menstruation or the completion of three months. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between puberty and maturity, emphasizing that the biological marker of menstruation, rather than age alone, determines the obligation of iddah in cases of consummated marriage. It reflects the practical application of Quranic principles regarding divorce procedures to minors, ensuring legal clarity for families in early marital arrangements.
